Energy (eV) and wavelength (nm) are related by  

 E (eV) = 1240 / λ (nm)  → λ = 1240 / E.

1. Emission energy given: 2.3393 eV  
 λ_emit = 1240 / 2.3393 ≈ 5.30 × 10² nm ≈ 530 nm, i.e. green light.

2. In fluorescence a molecule always absorbs a photon of slightly higher energy (shorter wavelength) than the one it later emits (Stokes shift).  
 Therefore the light absorbed must have a wavelength somewhat shorter than 530 nm.

3. Of the colors listed:
 • Yellow ≈ 580–590 nm (longer λ, lower E)  
 • Red  ≈ 620–750 nm (longer λ, lower E)  
 • Violet ≈ 380–450 nm (much shorter λ, much higher E)  
 • Blue  ≈ 450–495 nm (a bit shorter λ, moderately higher E)

The only reasonable, slightly higher-energy color just shorter than green is blue.

Answer: D
